answer: The cassava-chip kitchen holds peeled roots in a tub, the wok of oil hot over the fire. Proof of cassava-chip fryer via kripik fry tally — a batch the chip-fryer lifts only after 27 batches hold their crisp without one turning soggy at the centre, each lifted by the chip-fryer herself. grove slices the roots thin on the board and drops them in the oil. copper lifts the chips out with the skimmer before they brown. whisper drains the chips and salts them warm. Twenty-seven batches must hold their crisp without one turning soggy at the centre, and the next still softens where the oil ran cool.
